fields.title: New Staff Member shows Technician last in its own toggle row
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Start on Settings, Staff.
fields.custom_steps: 1. Open the New Staff Member window.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Staff Member window opens.
  • Below the Billable field there is a row holding only three toggles, in this order: Time Clock, Sales Representative, Technician.
  • The toggle labeled "Technician" is directly to the right of Sales Representative and is the last toggle in that row.
  • The Technician toggle is the same kind of switch as Time Clock and Sales Representative (same size, shape and colours).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Technician Toggle", Confluence 977371146, version 17 (2 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 2 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11788, story SV-11879 (Story 1, Technician toggle on a staff member)

  • S1-R1: “The New Staff Member and Edit Staff Member windows (Settings, Staff) show a toggle labeled "Technician" directly to the right of the Sales Representative toggle, as the last toggle in that row (Time Clock, Sales Representative, Technician). In both windows the three toggles share one row of their own, below the Billable field, so New and Edit look the same, in the same style as the window's other toggles.”
  • Key Decisions: “Technician is a toggle on each staff member, in the staff window next to Sales Representative.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Technician Toggle" (https://claude.ai/artifact/1fuPz8Y4xTg7Syq1mfmJ9R), version 1793629882-06f7, read 2 Nov 2026: page "2 Turn Technician on for a staff member", pictures "New Staff Member" (This build) and "New Staff Member" (Production today (before))

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • tt-p2-02-after-new-staff-member.png
  • tt-p2-01-before-new-staff-member.png

The design's own words:

  • “The three toggles move to one row of their own below Billable, the same row as Edit: Time Clock, Sales Representative, Technician. Nothing else moves.”
  • “Technician is last, with the "New" pill (same end date as the staff list pill). The window opens with no role and Time Clock off, so Technician starts off and grayed out.”
  • “Time Clock and Sales Representative sit beside Billable. No Technician toggle.”

fields.title: Edit Staff Member shows the same toggle row as New Staff Member
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have any active staff member, staff member A.
  • Start on Settings, Staff.
fields.custom_steps: 1. Open staff member A's Edit Staff Member window.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Edit Staff Member window opens.
  • Below the Billable field there is a row holding only three toggles, in this order: Time Clock, Sales Representative, Technician.
  • The row is in the same place and order as in the New Staff Member window.
  • The "Technician" label carries a "New" pill at its top right.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Technician Toggle", Confluence 977371146, version 17 (2 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 2 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11788, story SV-11879 (Story 1, Technician toggle on a staff member)

  • S1-R1: “The New Staff Member and Edit Staff Member windows (Settings, Staff) show a toggle labeled "Technician" directly to the right of the Sales Representative toggle, as the last toggle in that row (Time Clock, Sales Representative, Technician). In both windows the three toggles share one row of their own, below the Billable field, so New and Edit look the same, in the same style as the window's other toggles.”
  • S1-R2: “A "New" pill sits at the top right of the "Technician" label, touching the end of the word. It looks the same as the pill on the Work Orders display switcher. It shows until 07:00 UTC on the seventh day after the release that ships this feature, then disappears for everyone, including in a window that is already open.   • tt-p2-04-before-edit-staff-member.png

  • “Technician is off: on release day it was turned on only for people who, in the last 90 days, had time on a work order, lead or are on a line of an open work order, or are billable. She was none of those.”

fields.title: New Staff Member pre-fills Technician on for the Technician role
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Start on Settings, Staff.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open the New Staff Member window.
  2. If Time Clock is off, switch it on.
  3. In Role, pick "Technician".
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Staff Member window opens.

Step 2:

  • Time Clock is on.

Step 3:

  • Role shows Technician.
  • Technician switches on by itself, without being switched by hand.
  • Technician is not grayed out.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Technician Toggle", Confluence 977371146, version 18 (2 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 2 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11788, story SV-11879 (Story 1, Technician toggle on a staff member), story SV-11884 (Story 6, Release day)

  • S1-R3: “In the New Staff Member window, Technician is pre-filled from the role shown: on when the role is the built-in Technician or the built-in Foreman role and Time Clock is on, otherwise off. Every other role pre-fills off, including Parts Technician and every custom role, even one made from Technician or Foreman. The pre-fill runs when the window opens and again each time the role or Time Clock is changed, until the user switches Technician by hand. From then on the user's choice wins: changing the role or Time Clock no longer pre-fills it, though S1-R4 and S1-N1 still turn it off, and only the user turns it back on. The toggle as shown is what is saved. Save & Add Next clears the form as it does today (no role, Time Clock off, Technician off) and forgets any earlier switch by hand, so the next person is pre-filled from their own role. Edit Staff Member never pre-fills (S1-E1).”
  • Key Decisions: “New staff start with Technician set from their role: on for the built-in Technician and Foreman roles, off for every other role.”
  • Goals: “Existing shops need no setup: release day sets the toggle from recent work. New staff on the built-in Technician or Foreman role start on; everyone else starts off, so a parts or office hire never lands on the board by accident.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Technician Toggle" (https://claude.ai/artifact/1fuPz8Y4xTg7Syq1mfmJ9R), version 1793640819-ff4d, read 2 Nov 2026: page "2 Turn Technician on for a staff member", picture "Technician role picked" (This build)

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • tt-p2-03-after-technician-role-picked.png

The design's own words:

  • “Time Clock on and the built-in Technician role picked: Technician switches on by itself. The built-in Foreman role does the same; every other role, including Parts Technician and custom roles, leaves it off.”
  • “Changing the role or Time Clock sets it again from the role, until the user switches Technician by hand: from then on their choice wins. Edit Staff Member never does this.”

AUTOMATION: Not available on Build to test Yet - Last checked 11/2/2026

  • Technician is off and grayed out.
  • Clicking the Technician toggle does not switch it on.

Step 4:

  • A tooltip shows "Turn on Time Clock first. Only staff who clock in can be technicians."

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Technician Toggle", Confluence 977371146, version 18 (2 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 2 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11788, story SV-11879 (Story 1, Technician toggle on a staff member)

  • S1-R4: “Technician can only be on while Time Clock is on. While Time Clock is off, the Technician toggle is off and grayed out, and hovering it shows "Turn on Time Clock first. Only staff who clock in can be technicians." Turning Time Clock off, in the window or any other way (for example through the Public API), turns Technician off.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Hover the grayed-out Technician toggle while Time Clock is off (S1-R4) | "Turn on Time Clock first. Only staff who clock in can be technicians." | Tooltip while hovering”
  • Key Decisions: “Who is a technician is defined by two things only: the person's Technician toggle and their Time Clock. Technician needs Time Clock: it cannot be on while Time Clock is off.”
  • Story 1, Error Handling: “The window never sends Technician on without Time Clock, or for a staff member on the built-in Office User or Time Clock User role. A request from elsewhere (for example a second tab, or a staff window opened before another user changed the record) that would switch Technician from off to on in either case is refused with "A technician must have Time Clock on." or "This role can't be a technician." respectively, shown through the existing request error behavior, and nothing is saved. The Public API cannot set Technician, so it never gets these messages (S5-N1). When both apply (Time Clock off and one of those roles), the message is "This role can't be a technician.", both on hover in the window and in the refusal. A request for a staff member whose Technician is already on that turns Time Clock off, or moves them to one of those roles, is not refused: it saves, and Technician turns off (S1-R4, S1-N1).”

fields.title: Save & Add Next starts the next person fresh and forgets a hand switch
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Choose names and email addresses for two new staff members made by this test.
  • Start on Settings, Staff.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open the New Staff Member window.
  2. Type a first name in the first name field.
  3. Type a last name in the last name field.
  4. Type an email address that no other staff member uses in the email field.
  5. Fill in any other field the window marks as required.
  6. If Time Clock is off, switch it on.
  7. In Role, pick "Technician".
  8. Switch Technician off.
  9. Click Save & Add Next.
  10. Switch Time Clock on.
  11. In Role, pick "Technician".
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Staff Member window opens.

Step 2:

  • The first name shows.

Step 3:

  • The last name shows.

Step 4:

  • The email address shows.

Step 5:

  • No required field is left empty.

Step 6:

  • Time Clock is on.

Step 7:

  • Technician switches on by itself.

Step 8:

  • Technician is off (switched by hand).

Step 9:

  • The first staff member is saved and the window stays open with an empty form.
  • The empty form shows no role, Time Clock off and Technician off.

Step 10:

  • Time Clock is on.
  • Technician is still off (no role is picked yet).

Step 11:

  • Role shows Technician.
  • Technician switches on by itself: the first person's switch by hand was forgotten.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Technician Toggle", Confluence 977371146, version 18 (2 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 2 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11788, story SV-11879 (Story 1, Technician toggle on a staff member)

  • S1-R3: “In the New Staff Member window, Technician is pre-filled from the role shown: on when the role is the built-in Technician or the built-in Foreman role and Time Clock is on, otherwise off. Every other role pre-fills off, including Parts Technician and every custom role, even one made from Technician or Foreman. The pre-fill runs when the window opens and again each time the role or Time Clock is changed, until the user switches Technician by hand. From then on the user's choice wins: changing the role or Time Clock no longer pre-fills it, though S1-R4 and S1-N1 still turn it off, and only the user turns it back on. The toggle as shown is what is saved. Save & Add Next clears the form as it does today (no role, Time Clock off, Technician off) and forgets any earlier switch by hand, so the next person is pre-filled from their own role. Edit Staff Member never pre-fills (S1-E1).”
  • Key Decisions: “New staff start with Technician set from their role: on for the built-in Technician and Foreman roles, off for every other role.”

From: Chris Ward's answers, Google Sheet "Technician Toggle – questions for Chris Ward (2 Nov 2026)", https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1nLKkgSgmtqCYu4eu15_9xN38ml32tDnJls42PPq_A4M, column E, answered 2 Nov 2026 (po-answers-2026-11-02/ANSWERS-Chris-Ward-2026-11-02.md), read 2 Nov 2026

  • Answer 8 (question 8): “8. (a) As if the window had just opened. Save & Add Next clears the form the same way it does today: no role, Time Clock off, Technician off. Any earlier switch by hand is forgotten, and the next person's Technician is set from their own role. I'll add Save & Add Next to S1-R3.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Technician Toggle" (https://claude.ai/artifact/1fuPz8Y4xTg7Syq1mfmJ9R), version 1793640819-ff4d, read 2 Nov 2026: page "2 Turn Technician on for a staff member", pictures "New Staff Member" (This build) and "Technician role picked" (This build)

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • tt-p2-02-after-new-staff-member.png
  • tt-p2-03-after-technician-role-picked.png

The design's own words:

  • “The three toggles move to one row of their own below Billable, the same row as Edit: Time Clock, Sales Representative, Technician. Nothing else moves.”
  • “Technician is last, with the "New" pill (same end date as the staff list pill). The window opens with no role and Time Clock off, so Technician starts off and grayed out.”
  • “Time Clock on and the built-in Technician role picked: Technician switches on by itself. The built-in Foreman role does the same; every other role, including Parts Technician and custom roles, leaves it off.”
  • “Changing the role or Time Clock sets it again from the role, until the user switches Technician by hand: from then on their choice wins. Edit Staff Member never does this.”
  • “Save & Add Next starts the next person fresh: no role, Time Clock off, Technician off, and any earlier switch by hand is forgotten.”

Ruled: Chris answered question 8 (a): Save & Add Next starts the next person as if the window had just opened (register TT-D06, PO-RULED); the design's page 2 note now says the same.

fields.title: An old staff window that turns Technician on without Time Clock is refused
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have a new staff member for this test, staff member A, on the built-in Parts Manager role, with Time Clock on and Technician off, enrolled at the test location only, leading no work.
  • Start on Settings, Staff.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open staff member A's Edit Staff Member window.
  2. Open staff member A's Edit Staff Member window in a second browser tab.
  3. Switch Time Clock off.
  4. Click Save & Close.
  5. Switch to the first browser tab.
  6. Switch Technician on.
  7. Click Save & Close.
  8. Reload the page.
  9. Open staff member A's Edit Staff Member window.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The window shows Time Clock on and Technician off.

Step 2:

  • The second tab shows the same window.

Step 3:

  • Time Clock is off in the second tab.

Step 4:

  • The second tab's window closes and the change is saved.

Step 5:

  • The first tab still shows the old window: Time Clock on and Technician off.

Step 6:

  • Technician is on in this old window.

Step 7:

  • The save is refused with "A technician must have Time Clock on.", shown the way the app shows a refused save today.
  • The window does not close.

Step 8:

  • The staff list loads again.

Step 9:

  • Technician is off: nothing from the refused save was kept.
  • The change saved in the second tab is still there.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Technician Toggle", Confluence 977371146, version 18 (2 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 2 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11788, story SV-11879 (Story 1, Technician toggle on a staff member)

  • Story 1, Error Handling: “The window never sends Technician on without Time Clock, or for a staff member on the built-in Office User or Time Clock User role. A request from elsewhere (for example a second tab, or a staff window opened before another user changed the record) that would switch Technician from off to on in either case is refused with "A technician must have Time Clock on." or "This role can't be a technician." respectively, shown through the existing request error behavior, and nothing is saved. The Public API cannot set Technician, so it never gets these messages (S5-N1). When both apply (Time Clock off and one of those roles), the message is "This role can't be a technician.", both on hover in the window and in the refusal. A request for a staff member whose Technician is already on that turns Time Clock off, or moves them to one of those roles, is not refused: it saves, and Technician turns off (S1-R4, S1-N1).”
  • User Feedback Summary: “A request turns Technician on without Time Clock (S1 Error Handling) | "A technician must have Time Clock on." | Existing request error behavior”

From: Chris Ward's answers, Google Sheet "Technician Toggle – questions for Chris Ward (2 Nov 2026)", https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1nLKkgSgmtqCYu4eu15_9xN38ml32tDnJls42PPq_A4M, column E, answered 2 Nov 2026 (po-answers-2026-11-02/ANSWERS-Chris-Ward-2026-11-02.md), read 2 Nov 2026

  • Answer 1 (question 1): “1. (a) Accepted, and the Technician value is ignored. Outside tools can read Technician through the Public API but can't set it in this release (S5-N1). The two refusal messages only come from ShopView's own staff window, for example a second tab with old data. I'll fix the "outside tool" example in Story 1 Error Handling so it says that.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

Step 2:

  • The Technician toggle is off.

Step 3:

  • The warning window titled "Turn Off Technician" shows, with a Cancel button and a Save button.
  • Its text reads "[staff member A's first and last name] leads 1 open work order. They'll stay on it, but won't be offered as a technician on anything new."

In the warning texts, [staff member A's first and last name] stands for staff member A's name exactly as it was last saved.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Technician Toggle", Confluence 977371146, version 17 (2 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 2 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11788, story SV-11880 (Story 2, Warning before turning Technician off)

  • S2-R3, 1 work order, no lines: “1 work order, no lines: "[Name] leads 1 open work order. They'll stay on it, but won't be offered as a technician on anything new."”
  • S2-R2: “When at least one work order or line is counted, a warning window titled "Turn Off Technician" shows. The text names the staff member as last saved (a new name typed in the same save is not used) and what they hold, for example: "Jordan Lee leads 8 open work orders and is on 50 labor lines. They'll stay on them, but won't be offered as a technician on anything new."”
  • S2-R1: “When the user saves, before anything else, the system counts the staff member's open work across every location of the organization: the work orders they lead and the lines they are on, whether they have labor on the line, were added to it with Add Technician, or are the line's own technician, where the work order is a service work order in Estimate, Approved, In Progress or Ready for Review and the line is not declined. Preconditions

  • Have a new staff member for this test, staff member A, on the built-in Parts Manager role, with Time Clock on and Technician off, enrolled at the test location only.

fields.custom_steps: 1. Reload the Board View page.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Staff member B has a column.
  • Staff member A has no column, although their Time Clock is on.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Technician Toggle", Confluence 977371146, version 18 (2 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 2 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11788, story SV-11881 (Story 3, Who appears on the technician lists)

  • S3-R2: “Board View gives a column, and Tech View a group, to each person offered by S3-R1, plus everyone who leads work shown on the board (S3-E1, S3-E2).”
  • S3-N1: “A person with Technician off, or with Time Clock off, gets no Board View column, no Tech View group, and is not offered in the Technician filter or any technician dropdown, unless S3-E1 or S3-E2 applies. A person already picked in the Technician filter who is no longer offered (Technician turned off, or a person from another location) is dropped from the filter the next time the board loads, as if never picked. Their work orders do not move.”
  • S3-R1: “A person is offered on a technician list at a location when all of these hold: their Technician toggle is on, their Time Clock is on, their user is active, they are enrolled at that location, and their role is not the built-in Office User or Time Clock User role.”
  • Terminology: “Technician lists → Board View columns, Tech View groups, the Technician filter on Work Orders, the Assign / Reassign lead technician window, the Lead Technician dropdown on a work order, Add Technician on a line, and the Technician dropdown in the Edit Labor window. Nothing else.”
  • Goals: “A shop can take a Parts Manager (or anyone who is not a technician) off Board View, Tech View and every technician dropdown while that person keeps clocking in.”

Expected Result

Step 1:

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R10: “When Board View or Tech View has no technician column or group at all (no technician at the location, no column kept for a non-technician lead under S3-E1 and no pinned column under S3-E2), and neither Assigned to me nor a Technician filter is on, it shows the title "No technicians yet" with the text "Turn Technician on for your technicians in Staff to assign work orders. Until then, every work order stays in Unassigned." A Technician filter can be on at such a location only through its Unassigned or Deleted technician choices: people picked at another location are dropped from the filter when the location changes (S3-N1). When the open tab has no work orders either, the "Nothing here yet" state keeps its title, and its text reads "Turn Technician on for your technicians and create your first work order to track work by tech." The button the Board View and Tech View PRD (S1-N1d, SV-11555) calls Add Technician reads "Set Up Technicians" and opens the staff list (Settings, Staff), for the same users who see it today. This replaces S1-N1d's text and button target once this feature ships.”

From: Chris Ward's answers, Google Sheet "Technician Toggle – questions for Chris Ward (2 Nov 2026)", https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1nLKkgSgmtqCYu4eu15_9xN38ml32tDnJls42PPq_A4M, column E, answered 2 Nov 2026 (po-answers-2026-11-02/ANSWERS-Chris-Ward-2026-11-02.md), read 2 Nov 2026
